items.title: Starry Night Motion Blur Portrait
items.prompt: Preserve the face from the source photo: features, proportions, natural asymmetry, hair colour, skin tone. Face is softened by strong motion blur and out-of-focus blur at the same time, but the silhouette and features match the source. Ignore everything else from the source photo: background, clothing, pose, angle, lighting, composition. Night in a remote location far from city lights. The sky fills most of the frame — a dense scatter of stars, the glowing band of the Milky Way clearly visible running diagonally across the sky, a faint haze of nebulae. A dark horizon below, distant hill silhouettes barely visible. She stands facing the camera. The moment: a sudden gust of wind hits her — her body sways slightly, her head turns, the motion not yet settled. Her face is blurry for two combined reasons: the camera missed focus on her (out-of-focus blur) AND she moved during the shot (motion blur from the sudden gust). Both effects stack together — her face is soft, unfocused, and streaked in the direction of the movement. Facial contours double, features softened and generalized, no single point sharp. Still, the head silhouette and overall expression are guessable, the face stays recognizable by general shape, the features remain correct and attractive. Hair flew apart into long powerful blurred trails from the wind. Her face is lit by a soft warm light from below and in front — like a flashlight or small ground-level source — this light picks her out of the darkness, while the sky behind her stays completely dark and starry, not overexposed. Expression: a warm live smile, lips parted, corners raised — readable through the blur. Not a serious face. Clothing: {argument name="outfit" default="a long flowing slip dress in deep emerald silk"}, thin straps, the hem catching the wind and blurred by the motion, the dark fabric dissolving into the night. The "Immutable" Container (The Vinyl Stage): The Base: Each diorama is built on top of a Spinning Vinyl Record acting as the circular stage floor. Text Rule: It must clearly display the [ARTIST NAME] in bold, legible, capital letters. 3. The Composition (The Sound Made Solid): CRITICAL: Do not just recreate the album cover. Build a world that feels like the music. The Structure: Architecture rises from the grooves of the vinyl record. Example: A wall of amplifiers, a surreal floating prism, a crumbling brick wall, or a forest of microphone stands. The Atmosphere: Use particle effects to visualize the sound waves. Visuals: Floating musical notes made of smoke, vibrating liquid surfaces, or shattered glass suspended in mid-air. Background: Seamless Slate Grey to keep the focus on the colors. Output: 2x2 Grid, Hyper-Realistic Miniature Set Design, 8k Resolution, "Audiophile" Aesthetic.
